title: An Entity Extraction Pipeline for Medical Text Records Using Large Language Models: Analytical Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: The study of disease progression relies on clinical data, including text data, and extracting valuable features from text data has been a research hot spot. With the rise of large language models (LLMs), semantic-based extraction pipelines are gaining acceptance in clinical research. However, the security and feature hallucination issues of LLMs require further attention. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to introduce a novel modular LLM pipeline, which could semantically extract features from textual patient admission records. METHODS: The pipeline was designed to process a systematic succession of concept extraction, aggregation, question generation, corpus extraction, and question-and-answer scale extraction, which was tested via 2 low-parameter LLMs: Qwen-14B-Chat (QWEN) and Baichuan2-13B-Chat (BAICHUAN). A data set of 25,709 pregnancy cases from the People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China, was used for evaluation with the help of a local expert's annotation. The pipeline was evaluated with the metrics of accuracy and precision, null ratio, and time consumption. Additionally, we evaluated its performance via a quantified version of Qwen-14B-Chat on a consumer-grade GPU. RESULTS: The pipeline demonstrates a high level of precision in feature extraction, as evidenced by the accuracy and precision results of Qwen-14B-Chat (95.52% and 92.93%, respectively) and Baichuan2-13B-Chat (95.86% and 90.08%, respectively). Furthermore, the pipeline exhibited low null ratios and variable time consumption. The INT4-quantified version of QWEN delivered an enhanced performance with 97.28% accuracy and a 0% null ratio. CONCLUSIONS: The pipeline exhibited consistent performance across different LLMs and efficiently extracted clinical features from textual data. It also showed reliable performance on consumer-grade hardware. This approach offers a viable and effective solution for mining clinical research data from textual records.

claims.text: Qwen-14B-Chat achieved an average accuracy of 95.52% on 1,500 manually annotated clinical observations.
Qwen-14B-Chat achieved an average precision of 92.93% on 1,500 manually annotated clinical observations.
Baichuan2-13B-Chat achieved an average accuracy of 95.86% on 1,500 manually annotated clinical observations.
Baichuan2-13B-Chat achieved an average precision of 90.08% on 1,500 manually annotated clinical observations.
The INT4-quantified version of Qwen-14B-Chat achieved an average accuracy of 97.28% on the annotated test subset.
The INT4-quantified version of Qwen-14B-Chat achieved a 0% null ratio across all observations.
Qwen-14B-Chat recorded a mean null ratio of 0.02% across 25,709 clinical observations.
Baichuan2-13B-Chat recorded a mean null ratio of 0.21% across 25,709 clinical observations.
Executing Q&A scale extraction at a concurrency level of 3 requests increases extraction speed by 17.9% compared to a single request.
Omitting the corpus pre-extraction step leads to degraded accuracy, precision, and processing speed.

limitations.text: The experimental validation selected a limited set of only 68 concepts to balance execution time constraints.
Raw clinical patient data were sourced exclusively from a single hospital, which limits the generalizability of the findings.
The approach was evaluated using only two specific low-parameter Chinese LLM architectures (Qwen-14B-Chat and Baichuan2-13B-Chat).
Submitting patient data to non-open-source cloud LLM platforms introduces patient privacy and data security challenges.
Directly processing extensive unsegmented clinical text with LLMs frequently induces feature hallucinations and information loss.

future_work.text: Validate the compatibility and effectiveness of the modular extraction pipeline across emerging and broader LLM architectures.
Explore multi-instance deployment strategies per GPU combined with CPU execution to scale processing speeds for large clinical cohorts.

methodologies.name: External Chain-of-Thought Modular LLM Extraction Pipeline
methodologies.description: A four-stage framework that decomposes clinical feature extraction into concept preparation, corpus pre-extraction, question generation, and Q&A scale extraction using local low-parameter open-source LLMs.
datasets: 25,709 pregnancy admission records from People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region
conditions: NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU for INT4 quantized variant
